subject: Temporary exemption request: dedicated slate for live ops burst
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary exemption request: dedicated slate for live ops burst

Team —

CardioCloud (pilot customer) has just confirmed a surprise live ops event they want to run next week: an internal product demo to a potential buyer that will route ~2.5x our normal inference QPS for a 6 hour window. They are under a short contractual deadline tied to the pilot (deal CC-2028-PILOT).

Ask: Can we grant a temporary exemption to the autoscale floor/eviction policy and carve a dedicated slate (private pool slice) for the 6-hour window on 2028-03-29 UTC 16:00-22:00? The slice would be isolated to the CardioCloud pilot, with a strict eviction guard afterwards.

Operational constraints I know: we need a runbook, an override on the autoscaler, and a billing note for the customer. I attached a short burst_plan.xlsx with expected token rates and the rough instance sizing. Also linking the JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-1345 and a draft folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cexample

Immediate next steps I need from you:
- Kimberly: confirm whether an exception to the eviction/soft-preempt policy is feasible for a 6-hour window and what guardrails we can enforce.
- Marcus/Dev: estimate the config changes to autonome autoscale policy and how long a rollback will take.
- I'll loop in Contracts and the CardioCloud contacts once we have the ops footprint.

Time sensitivity: CardioCloud needs a final answer by EOD Thursday (2028-03-24) so they can update the execs.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary exemption request: dedicated slate for live ops burst

Tessa —

Thanks for flagging. Short answer: yes, we can support a controlled temporary exemption, but we need to lock three things before sign-off:

1) Exact capacity numbers (vGPU count / expected average and peak seq length). The attached burst_plan.xlsx helps but the more precise the input the less conservative we need to be.
2) A rollback plan that can be triggered automatically if host-level contention rises beyond threshold. We usually set a 15-minute monitoring window + auto-evict if 95th percentile latency jumps > 30%.
3) Billing and ticketing: we need Contracts to approve a one-off surcharge and the customer to sign the SLA addendum.

Operational notes:
- We can create a temporary slate (slice id will be SLICE-CC-03-29) and pin it to a dedicated GPU pool.
- Autoscale override: we can add an override flag that bumps min-instances for the slice for the requested window; rollback is a single API call and should be < 5 mins once we push it.
- Eviction guard: we can enable a hard-eviction protect timer so the slice can't be preempted for the 6-hour window, but it will be automatically cleared afterwards.

Marcus/Dev — can you validate that the SLICE creation + override + rollback can be completed in the 24–48 hour lead time? If yes, I can draft the technical runbook.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa/Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming CardioCloud is comfortable signing an SLA addendum for the one-off event. Our expected characteristics:
- Peak concurrency window: 45 minutes within the 6-hour window (demo + Q&A), peak QPS estimate: +2.5x baseline.
- Approx token mix: short prompts (<= 120 tokens) and a small set of long-form reports (avg 800 tokens) for 10% of calls.

Attached is the signed SLA_addendum.pdf (scanned). We can also take the surcharge on the pilot if Redwood prefers a credit-line billing and retro reconciliation.

Please let us know the slice id and the exact time you will flip the override so our embed side is ready.

Best,

Perfect — thanks all. Quick plan & owners: 

- Marcus: provision SLICE-CC-03-29 (dedicated pool) and confirm instance counts by EOD 2028-03-23. Use the sizing in burst_plan.xlsx as baseline; be conservative on long-form requests.
- Dev: prepare the autoscale-override toggle + rollback playbook (override-runbook.md attached). Test the rollback path in staging and report time to rollback.
- Kimberly: draft the short ops runbook with monitoring thresholds and the 15-minute auto-evict guard.
- Contracts/Olivia: thanks for the addendum — once we have the slice id we will share the scheduled flip time.

I'll log the approval in JIRA-OPS-1345 and will send a final confirmation to CardioCloud by 2028-03-24 EOD. After the window we'll run a short postmortem (10–15m) and reconcile billing.

Attachments referenced: burst_plan.xlsx, override-runbook.md, SLA_addendum.pdf
